nodes.title: feat: add sortKeys option for sorting object keys in output
nodes.body:
## Summary

Adds a `sortKeys` option that controls the order of object keys in prettified log output.

Closes #107

## Usage

```js
// Ascending (alphabetical) order
const pretty = prettyFactory({ sortKeys: true })

// Descending order
const pretty = prettyFactory({ sortKeys: 'desc' })

// Custom comparator
const pretty = prettyFactory({
  sortKeys: (a, b) => a.length - b.length
})
```

CLI:
```bash
cat logs | pino-pretty --sortKeys
cat logs | pino-pretty --sortKeys desc
```

## Changes

- `index.js` — add `sortKeys` to default options and JSDoc
- `lib/utils/parse-factory-options.js` — pass `sortKeys` through to context
- `lib/utils/prettify-object.js` — sort `Object.entries()` before iteration when `sortKeys` is set
- `README.md` — document the new option
- `test/basic.test.js` — 3 new tests covering `true`, `'desc'`, and custom comparator

## Tests

```
node --test test/basic.test.js

# tests 76
# pass 76
# fail 0
```

nodes.title: fix: substitute conditional messageFormat values literally
fix: support nested timestampKey and messageKey paths
nodes.body:
## Summary

Fixes #438.

`levelKey` already supports nested and escaped property paths. `timestampKey` and `messageKey` still used top-level access, so timestamps and messages under Pino `nestedKey` objects (for example, `nested_key.time`) were ignored.

This PR gives `timestampKey` and `messageKey` the same path rules, removes rendered nested values from the remaining object dump, and preserves the existing behavior of top-level keys.

## Root cause and fix

- Resolve nested timestamp/message paths with the existing split/get helpers.
- Delete already-rendered nested paths from the object dump and prune empty parents.
- Return `undefined` instead of throwing when an intermediate path value is `null` or `undefined`.
- Preserve legacy `key in log` behavior only for a single top-level segment; nested paths remain own-property-only.
- Document nested and escaped `--timestampKey` / `--messageKey` paths.

The last two points close compatibility gaps found during follow-up self-review:

- `{ meta: null }` with `timestampKey: 'meta.time'` and `{ payload: null }` with `messageKey: 'payload.text'` previously threw a `TypeError` on the PR branch.
- `Object.create({ time: 123, msg: 'inherited' })` had stopped rendering the inherited top-level values even though the current release renders `[123] INFO: inherited`.

## Verification

- [x] Target unit/integration tests: 129/129
- [x] All tests except the Windows `cli-rc.test.js` subprocess case: 365/365
- [x] Coverage gate on those 365 tests: 100%
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm run test:types`: 66/66 assertions; ATTW package checks green
- [x] Manual regression matrix: nested time/message, escaped paths, missing paths, `time: 0`, `null` parents, inherited top-level keys, and no duplicate nested values in the object dump

The full `npm run ci` command still hangs in the existing `cli-rc.test.js` child-process case on this Windows host. That test is unrelated to the touched paths; it was excluded explicitly above rather than reported as passing. GitHub has not scheduled CI checks for this fork PR.

## Notes

- No force-pushes were used. Compatibility fixes and the LF normalization are separate follow-up commits.
- The final PR diff contains no whole-file line-ending churn.

nodes.title: fix: preserve large integer precision in pretty output
nodes.body:
Fixes #633

## Summary

- Preserve the exact decimal token for integers outside the safe JavaScript `Number` range.
- Keep BigInt values serializable in object, nested, array, and single-line output paths.
- Add BigInt epoch handling and regression tests for the reported case and numeric boundaries.

## Root cause

Pino serializes `BigInt` values as bare JSON integers. `JSON.parse` converts those tokens to `Number` before `pino-pretty` formats them, so values above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are rounded (for example, `1666666666666666700` becomes `1666666666666666800`).

The reviver uses `context.source` to recover the original integer token and stores it as `BigInt`. `safe-stable-stringify` is used for the object formatter because the existing `fast-safe-stringify` path cannot serialize BigInt values. Its non-deterministic configuration preserves the formatter's existing insertion-order output and circular-reference handling.

A bare unsafe integer has the same JSON representation whether it originated as a BigInt or an unsafe JavaScript Number, so the parser preserves the exact token for both cases.

## Verification

- `npm test`
- `npx eslint lib test --ignore-pattern 'test/.tmp_*'`
- `npm run test:types`
- `git diff --check`

nodes.title: feat: colorize JSON output in single-line mode (#229)
nodes.body:
Fixes #229.

### Summary

In `singleLine` mode, syntax-highlight serialized JSON object payloads by token type instead of wrapping the entire payload in a single grey color.

### Key changes

- Add an internal JSON tokenizer/highlighter that uses pino-pretty's active Colorette color functions and preserves unrecognized characters verbatim.
- Apply token highlighting in single-line object rendering while retaining a fallback for custom colorizers that do not implement `.json()`.
- Add unit, integration, regression, and type tests for token colors, escaping, nested values, no-color modes, and compatibility.

### Compatibility

- `colorize: false` and `colorizeObjects: false` remain ANSI-free.
- Explicit colorization continues to work in piped/non-TTY output.
- Multi-line object formatting remains unchanged.
- No new runtime dependency or lockfile change.

### Verification

- `npm test`: 394 passed, 0 failed
- `npm run lint`: passed
- `npm run test:types`: passed
- `npm run ci`: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
